parts:
Dear all, 

For my PhD thesis, I am going to analyse sleep and PA data from app. 200 participants, who have been wearing GeneActive accelerometer for 5 * 7 days. This means that I have around 1,000 files to analyse. Since I do not have a cluster machine available, I'll be running these analyses on my "standard PC". 

I've put the files for analysis in 5 different folders based on measurement period (A1, A2, A3, A4, A5), and then I have one folder for the output from GGIR, in which I can see that GGIR automatically makes subfolders depending on measurement period (output_A1, output_A2, etc).  

Although the analysis probably runs faster than previously (thank you Vincent!), it takes time to do all 200 files at once. Therefore, I would prefer to run e.g. 20 or 30 files, and then the next 20-30 files, etc. 

However, yesterday I tried with the first ~50 files, but it "only" ran 46 files and then it stopped. 
Now, I try to analyse the 47th file, but now the Part 1 takes REALLY long time and the report for File 47 is not being created after this long waiting time. Neither, is the file included in the part2,4,5 summary files. Is there a limit of number of files? I guess, it should be possible to do more than 46 files, right?

Also, does anyone have some overall advises on how to organize the datadir and output folders, write the code, etc., when I do these analyses in smaller "bites" and for various measurement periods so that Part 1 does not take so long time the more analyses that I have been running? I have not changed the overwrite function, but maybe I should?

Hope someone can help me!? I have pasted in my R code and also the Console-text after running the analyses, where you can see that "Report part 2" only goes up to 39 (however, 46 files are included in the summaries) and "Generating visual reports" the next files (47th file) that I wanted to analyse is not being generated, neither is it included in the csv summary files.   

Also, if someone can help me what is wrong with some of the files (see Console errors/warnings):

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Max number of files? + Advises on how to run multiple analyses/files
parts:
Hi Charlotte, 
There is no limit on the number of files GGIR can process. GGIR has been used in data sets much larger than yours.
That said, more data will demand more memory, but with only 50 files I do not expect this to be a problem.

A more likely explanation is that you ran into a file that did not wanted to process at the report generations stage. This may indicate a bug in GGIR.

If the error message would occur earlier in the process you can investigate the issue by setting: overwrite =FALSE, do.parallel=FALSE... but in your case it probably does not help.
The other thing you can do is to investigate at what specific file the analysis stops. In other words what is file 47?
  • Can you process it as a separate dataset? 
  • Can you share the part 1 milestone data corresponding to file 47? (from the meta/basic/... folder).

General advise about processing large datasets:
  • Your approach of splitting the data is one way to do it. Another approach is to put all data in one folder with subfolders A1, A2, A3, etc and set argument storefolderstructure =TRUE. The nice thing then is that you get all your output in together in one csv overview, but there will be a column at the end indicating in which of the subfolders the file was stored.
  • Also you could use the f0 and f1 arguments to process specific subsets of the data.
  • Use overwrite=FALSE to process only the new files that have not been processed before.
  • I am not sure why more files would result in a slower process. Did you time the processing time and made sure that your PC is not trying to do other heavy tasks in parallel?
Best, Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees
Independent consultant
www.movementdata.nl

I think the package is running smoothly, thanks to Vicncet and his team. 

One suggestion, If it would be possible to calculate the time it need to process the data, it would be great. I remember reading about another package that can do that, but I can't remember the name. 

One last thing, if anyone has materials about interpreting the results, please let me know. 


Maher,

messages.author: 13568954e9b4ef4b
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Max number of files? + Advises on how to run multiple analyses/files
parts:
Process one file and measure the duration it, from that you can estimate how long the entire dataset takes.

If you have a laptop with 4 or more CPUs GGIR will try to process files in parallel. If you have many files there may be a point when doing your work on a dedicated computing cluster is a better option.

A general introduction can be found in the package vignette with further details in the CRAN pdf tutorial. Open Source software depends a lot from community contributions, so please feel free to contribute by proposing improvements to the documentation.
Thanks,
Vincent
